entities.summary:
Bubares (b. 600 BCE) was a religious figure or clergy of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Global. 


  Bubares was a prominent architect and engineer, known for his innovative designs in temples and public buildings, particularly in the city of Delphi, Greece.


  His work had a lasting impact on the development of Western architecture, influencing subsequent generations of architects and builders.


  The legacy of Bubares can be seen in the many ancient ruins that still stand today, testifying to his enduring contributions to the field of architecture.


  'The temple's design, as conceived by Bubares, remains a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of ancient Greek architects.'
